A KV cache stores the key and value tensors from previous token predictions for each generated token, enabling fast autoregressive generation by reusing these stored states instead of recomputing them during inference.

It typically holds a sequence of (key, value) pairs per layer/head across the context window, allowing the model to continue from prior hidden states without full forward passes.

answer-para2.content: When you send many small prompts to the same model in quick succession, each request forces the GPU to spin up and tear down kernels repeatedly, which wastes time on context‑switching and reduces overall throughput; by grouping those requests into a single batch, the framework can allocate a larger chunk of work to one or more streaming multiprocessors at once, allowing the hardware’s compute units to stay busy for longer periods. This amortizes the overhead of loading weights, managing memory, and synchronizing across threads, so each GPU core processes many tokens before the next request arrives. The result is higher arithmetic intensity per cycle, lower latency between requests, and a smoother pipeline that keeps the GPU saturated—essentially turning many tiny spikes into one steady flow of work, which dramatically boosts utilisation during LLM inference.
